activity_context.topic_title: Estimating Derivatives Using a Central Difference Quotient

feedback.problem: Given that $f(2.9)=5.91$ and $f(3.1)=7.11,$ find an approximation for ${f}^{′}(3).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=3$ with the step size $h=0.1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h} \\ {f}^{′}(3) & ≈\frac{f(3+0.1)-f(3-0.1)}{2(0.1)} \\  & =\frac{f(3.1)-f(2.9)}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{7.11-5.91}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{1.2}{0.2} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
